subject: Mutually Assured Destruction and the Path Forward…

body:
| | | | | [|

| | Friend,
I wanted to reach out personally because, if you’re paying attention to this race, you’re probably seeing exactly what we’re seeing.
While other campaigns are busy trading cheap shots, something important is getting lost: _**THE VOTERS**_.
As Patricia Murphy [recently wrote in the Atlanta Journal-Constitution](https://BradForGeorgia.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=cb0b5d8f4cac8238170f7992f&id=9fce07ebee&e=6036811227):
_“The danger for them, and for Republicans in general, is that, regardless of what is true and what isn’t, the Jackson and Jones campaigns seem hell-bent on destroying each other — even if it kills them both.”_
That’s not spin. That’s reality. And it creates a real opening.
Murphy goes on:
_“Voters I talk to want to hear what the candidates are for, not just who they’re against. But that’s not coming through for most Georgians right now.”_
**THAT is the opportunity in front of us...**
While Burt Jones and Rick Jackson burn millions tearing each other down, Brad is talking about how he is going to [build Georgia up](https://BradForGeorgia.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=cb0b5d8f4cac8238170f7992f&id=0dbd8f8468&e=6036811227) by...
* Lowering costs.
* Creating good-paying jobs.
* Backing law enforcement.
* Fixing education.

Georgia needs a leader, not someone focused solely on the fight instead of the future.
Murphy describes what’s happening between our opponents as:
_“The arms race of negative ads between Jackson and Jones is veering toward mutually assured destruction...nobody wins in that scenario.”_
In politics, when two candidates cancel each other out, a new pathway is created.
**THIS is Brad’s path forward...**
* Jones and Jackson split the same voters with overwhelmingly negative campaigns
* Their favorability declines as the attacks on one another intensify until one or both of them crack
* Republican voters look for a candidate who is conservative, steady, and solutions-oriented
* Brad consolidates voters looking for a real leader and secures a spot in the runoff

While others spend their money tearing down opponents, we’re investing in something stronger: a campaign built on real ideas, tested leadership, and a vision for Georgia’s future.
That’s where you come in.
We don't need to join the mudslinging to win. We need to keep spreading our message, building our campaign, and sharing our plan for a better Georgia with every voter in the state.
**And we need every supporter to chip in TODAY with a generous contribution of**[**$1000, $500, or even $50**](https://BradForGeorgia.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=cb0b5d8f4cac8238170f7992f&id=85919279e9&e=6036811227)**. Every dollar donated helps amplify our winning message.**
Thank you for standing with Brad and for choosing the path of dedicated leadership over the path of destruction.
Sincerely,
Team Brad
_P.S. The contrast in this race has never been clearer. Others are focused on each other. Brad is focused on Georgia. Let’s make sure voters know it._

body:
The opponents of voting rights funded by all this dark money know they can't win the argument on their own merits. They see voters rejecting their policies when the impact is fully explained.
That's why they create groups with generic names like "First Principles PAC," "The Lexington Fund," "Judicial Crisis Network," and "Honest Elections Project" to hide their true intent and drop millions of dollars into targeted elections.
It's going to take all of us to defend our right to vote from their onslaught. RUSH $35 or more right now to support our grassroots work to stop them >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=041526_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
NOTUS: ‘Dark Money’ Kingpin Leonard Leo Revamps Operation Ahead of Midterms [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=041526_2&amount=25]
Straight from NOTUS, folks:
" Conservative legal activist Leonard Leo’s 'dark money' operation is getting a makeover. " The article goes on to share details of the millions upon millions of dollars his dark money, suppressive network has spent over the years to impact judicial elections, voting rights, and so many other issues facing our country.
“ Because the names change, I think most Americans have no idea what’s going on or how many of these differently named groups are the same through line with Leonard Leo at the sort of center of the spider web, ” Lisa Graves, founder and executive director of the watchdog group True North Research, told NOTUS.
This is exactly what his movement is trying to accomplish. Confuse voters in targeted states using generic, patriotic-sounding names for groups specifically using billionaire money to take away their fundamental rights.
We're different. Our mission has been clear from day one: Increase voter participation through any means, specifically mail-in ballots. We've leveraged our grassroots power to inform Americans across the country and defend our fundamental right to vote. To keep fighting back against these suppressive, dark-money millions, we need your help .
Will you chip in $35 or whatever you can today to help us protect the right to vote and reach every voter we can ahead of the midterm elections? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=041526_2&amount=35]

We focus on meeting voters where they are , from young voters to voters of color to disabled voters who need mail-in ballots to cast a ballot.
With the ongoing threats to our right to vote and efforts to restrict access to the ballot, our work to mobilize these voters is more important than ever. That’s why we’re making it a priority to help potential new voters make a lifelong habit of voting, return lapsed voters to the process, and make sure long-term voters can still participate.
This work doesn't happen overnight , and getting people in every corner of the country excited to vote requires a lot of resources. We're working day and night in order to make a worthwhile investment and reach voters however we can.
The more people who vote, the more our government looks like what we, the people, want it to be. And that is much more than these dark money groups are fighting for.

But the truth is, all of that is on the line.
Democrats are already targeting this seat, and they are going to do everything they can to take it back.

So before anything else, I need to ask you something simple:
**Can I count on you in 2026?**

To keep this going, to keep taking the fight to Trump and demanding a better world, I’m asking for your help.
#

Friend,
Something that bothers me about this work is how many people seem to think there’s nothing we can do.
Nothing we can do to make dinner less expensive, or improve our schools, or make housing more affordable. Or worse, nothing we can do to stop a lawless president, and a Republican Congress that refuses to hold him accountable.
This kind of stuff used to be the minimum — and now, it’s like we’ve given up before we even gave it a shot. I refuse to accept that this is the best we can do, and I know you’re with me on that.
We’ve built a huge team working together on all of this and more. And I want you to know — it’s having a real impact. The tide is turning, but we can’t let up.
To keep this going, to keep taking the fight to Trump and demanding a better world, I’m asking for your help.

name: Teichert in the Trenches
subject: Dominating Through Debriefs
body:
Seventy-three years ago was the last time
---
| | | | | |
---
| | **💥****Dominating Through Debriefs****💥**
---
Seventy-three years ago (April 15, 1953) was the last time that an American military member on the ground was killed by a manned enemy aircraft from the air. That is an unmatched era of U.S. air dominance. What has led to such superiority?
Is it the amazing aircraft? In part, yes.
Is it the rigorous selection, training, and preparation of the pilots? In part, yes.
But, the essential element of our expertise is something applicable to all, whether or not your profession allows you to soar through the skies.
In every sortie I’ve flown, we’ve followed the same process. We did it in training, test, and combat. We start with mission planning and a pre-flight brief. In that brief, we go through the objectives of the mission and explain the details of how we intend to accomplish those objectives. Then we go out and execute.
The real magic happens when we get back from the flight. We debrief, and sometimes that debrief is as long as the duration of the mission, sometimes it’s twice as long, and sometimes it’s even longer than that.
In each case, we start with the objectives. Then we dissect the execution of the flight. Whenever we discover something that doesn’t meet our standards or expectations, we tirelessly seek out the root cause of the shortcoming. A proper debrief is characterized by dispassionate determination to learn, and a good flight lead is at least as rigorous in rooting out their own imperfections and they are in assessing the shortcomings of others.
As a result, we learn from each flight. We grow from each flight. We improve from each flight. And, we pass on that culture of rigorous, constant improvement to those who follow.
Leadership experts say that eighty to ninety percent of the time subordinates fall short, it’s because they haven’t been given clear expectations or regular feedback. In short, the workplace culture didn’t brief to objectives and assess against those objectives. When those failures happen, it’s primarily the leader’s fault.
The cycle of planning, briefing, execution, and debriefing must not be limited to the world of fast jets and those who live in the danger zone. Create your own cycle of explicit expectations and perpetual processes of red teams, hot washes, after action assessments, or debriefs. They don’t need to take long, but you need to infuse them into the culture of your team.
And when you do, you will find that you’ve created a culture of constant improvement. You and your teammates will learn. You will grow. You will improve. You will pass on that culture of rigorous constant improvement to those who follow.
As a result, you may even create your own seventy-three-year string of successes. Dominance through debriefs is a critical component of LEADING WELL!

* John

| | | | **Teichert in the Trenches**

clean_body: I really need you | | Dear Friend, I'm writing to you as a mother who is deeply worried about the world my children are growing up in. Every day, I see freedoms that I once took for granted being chipped away, replaced by rules and pressures that threaten the very values I want them to grow up with. It breaks my heart to think that my children may not have the same opportunities to live in a country that honors freedom, responsibility, and family. Every day, I am fighting to protect the liberties that my children deserve -- and the future of every child in this country. But I cannot do this alone. Your support today gives us the power to defend our schools, strengthen our communities, and ensure that the next generation grows up in a country that respects freedom and opportunity. Every moment we wait puts our children's future at risk. I'm asking you to stand with me -- to stand with all parents who want to protect the freedoms of their children. Please help me fight for the America our kids deserve. With hope and determination, Kathy Barnette Be Better America PAC | | PAID FOR BY BE BETTER AMERICA PAC Copyright (C) 2025 Be Better America PAC, All rights reserved.

# **Braun ****announces $200 million investment to help expand affordable child care in Indiana**
[Click Here to Read the Full Story](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ahykdlt-hhlljjcji-y/) Fox 59
David Gay
April 14, 2026
[https://fox59.com/indianapolitics/braun-announces-200-million-investment-to-help-expand-affordable-child-care-in-indiana/](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ahykdlt-hhlljjcji-j/)INDIANAPOLIS -- Officials with the office of Indiana Gov. Mike Braun announced that an investment of $200 million could be made to help expand affordable child care in the state of Indiana, pending review from the State Budget Committee.According to a news release from Braun's office, the committee is expected to review the investment of $200 million from the state's general fund into the Financial Responsibility and Opportunity Growth, or FROG, fund. If approved, this is expected to expand access to child care and development fund vouchers.The office expects that this funding would resume the enrollment of voucher-eligible children, increasing the number of enrollments by 14,000 to around 57,000."Indiana's child care voucher system is more than a support program -- it's an economic engine," Braun said in the release. "When parents have access to reliable, affordable child care, they can pursue better jobs, gain new skills and build stronger futures. And this investment isn't just for one year. It marks the start of a sustained commitment to keeping care affordable and giving families long-term confidence that the support they count on will remain in place. This investment strengthens our workforce while expanding opportunity for families."The release said that the siblings of current voucher holders, along with infants, toddlers, and 3-, 4-, and 5-year-olds, will be prioritized if the committee approves the investment. Exemptions will also be created for:
* Children of foster and kinship families
* Children with special needs
* Homeless children
* Children of child care workers
* Children of Ivy Tech students

"Every voucher is a commitment to a working family," Adam Alson, the director of the Indiana Office of Early Childhood and Out-of-School Learning with the Indiana Family and Social Services Administration, said in the release. "This investment allows us to reopen access after 15 months of frozen admissions, address the most urgent needs, and put Indiana on a sustainable path forward."The release said that under Braun's direction, the FSSA would implement "robust, ongoing anti-fraud safeguards - including a significant increase in site visits and enhanced provider oversight.""Such a significant investment in Indiana's Child Care and Development Fund is tremendous news for working families and the state's economy because no parent should have to choose between a paycheck and safe, reliable childcare," Indiana Chamber of Commerce President and CEO Vanessa Green Sinders said in the release. "This is also welcome action for Hoosier businesses, as childcare-related employee turnover and absenteeism costs employers over $3 billion annually. We look forward to partnering with the Governor and General Assembly on a sustainable funding model that keeps more Hoosiers in the workforce."Officials with the United Way of Central Indiana also praised Braun's announcement on Tuesday, stating that this "incredible investment in Indiana" will be "for today and tomorrow.""We anxiously await final approval by the State Budget Committee, so that Indiana's families and child care providers can once again focus on what matters most: the health and development of our youngest Hoosiers," Sam Sniderman, the vice president of government and sector relations for the United Way of Central Indiana, said in the statement.Indiana State Rep. Phil GiaQuinta, the Democratic leader in the Indiana House of Representatives, said in the statement that while he is thankful that Bruan has "taken steps to resuscitate" child care programs in the state of Indiana, he believes it was "too little, too late.""In December, House Democrats offered an opportunity for House Republicans to reject the redistricting bill and fund CCDF vouchers for a year. They said no," GiaQuinta said in the statement. "In last year's budget, Statehouse Republicans prioritized expanding private K-12 vouchers to Indiana's wealthiest families instead of funding child care and getting our neediest working families off the waitlist."I say all this not to descend into the partisan bickering that I know Hoosiers are tired of. I say this to let Hoosiers know that the near-collapse of our child care system is an active decision that Statehouse Republicans made time and time again," GiaQuinta continued. "The money has always been there - the question has been whether there is the political will to invest in the hard-working, low-income families that keep our state economy running." body:
| | | Hi Peter, You’re angry. You should be. **We all should be.** What’s happening across the country – to immigrants, to trans people, to women, and more – and beyond our borders in the countries we're starting wars with, from the rising prices and the slashing of critical services to the attacks on our elections and dismantling of our democracy, is unconscionable. It's also deliberate and strategic. And **the people doing it are counting on us to be overwhelmed** , to tune out, and to let them get away with it. **We won't.** I’m Amanda Gonzalez, and I’m running for Colorado Secretary of State because I know how to fight this fight. We’ve already been doing it. And we're gaining ground. I run elections for nearly half a million people in Jefferson County right now. I’m an election lawyer. I’ve written several of our election laws and helped pass even more. I've foiled election deniers. Upgraded election security. Made it possible for thousands of eligible voters in jail to cast a ballot. That’s not a promise about what I might do someday. It’s what I’ve already done. The next Secretary of State doesn’t have time for on-the-job training. The fight is already here.**Colorado needs someone who is already in it and knows how to win.** I’m not asking you to trust me from the sidelines, I’m asking you to join me in a fight that's well underway. Between now and June 30, hundreds of thousands of voters will be making up their minds about who should be entrusted with defending our democracy. body:
I have plans that will actually support American agriculture—but Republicans will fight me tooth and nail to stop it from succeeding.
| | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001j2GdxzC0Qsh05YR8Wll2lfQ4DzKNSbKO4je0Iwce9k_6M2n_j-avxALfUc06AmIsvuMq7eMSPHn96j_-zSh5sV6AirdGID4Pk8sXx4gUtpRnIIsL-wEt8UoeeQSAzEhIERrIHUEDqGAaLtAdkyfDjtsuPFzAV0zqwMuFwlAS25HlXp7Mdk65UqNY6kP0Pg2BrmxhpXv-8g6thauw59nWqJbJYmmNYxgn&c=1U2vbJ-_A1el264TADxNx_XOtt6bp5POtXvl6EW1Nu3PeKg8lS1BrA==&ch=kjvpm-xlUeJOzDGo3wQXmZPt6RfwKaqaaiFn4VftIX04DWbZsbY7uQ==)
---
| Peter,
I am a damn good farmer. Being a farmer is a calling, and I'm proud to have made this my life's work.
This is Jamie Davis, the Democrat running for US Senate in Louisiana. Three generations of my family have worked the Delta land that my son and I now own, much of the same acreage that my ancestors worked as sharecroppers.
It takes a ton of hard work and calculated risk to do this--but MAGA is making this impossible now. If we were just starting out today, my family and I would never be able to make it.
Trump's Agriculture Secretary, Brooke Rollins, said that "over 80%" of American farmers have already locked in prices for the fertilizer they need to plant right now. This is a boldfaced lie: farmers I know are not prepared for the massive shock coming from the price of fertilizer.
Data disproves it too. The Farm Bureau ran a survey just a few days ago that found most farmers report they are completely unprepared for the massive increase in prices for fertilizer and fuel--and over 78% of farmers in the South, including my state of Louisiana, are totally unable to afford what they need to plant their crops right now.

| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001j2GdxzC0Qsh05YR8Wll2lfQ4DzKNSbKO4je0Iwce9k_6M2n_j-avxALfUc06AmIsvuMq7eMSPHn96j_-zSh5sV6AirdGID4Pk8sXx4gUtpRnIIsL-wEt8UoeeQSAzEhIERrIHUEDqGAaLtAdkyfDjtsuPFzAV0zqwMuFwlAS25HlXp7Mdk65UqNY6kP0Pg2BrmxhpXv-8g7iCchV5lWu8j2a6kkXXh8l&c=1U2vbJ-_A1el264TADxNx_XOtt6bp5POtXvl6EW1Nu3PeKg8lS1BrA==&ch=kjvpm-xlUeJOzDGo3wQXmZPt6RfwKaqaaiFn4VftIX04DWbZsbY7uQ==)

## Iran Threatens to Block Trade Across Persian Gulf
Iran threatened Wednesday to [fully block exports and imports](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGu3CAQxvHT4A4LMIvtgmIbdxspVdJZgxmvJ8JgAbvW5vSR847w6r80mt_36zE_gALF5w_Y0dY1zRHPErBWzDNliHXLCLVsmNORKS50QIBZCWW40Fya2QOFz6wbb1dEhV2DVva96bpu7Idms04vt3XxcpGLd72TuGhhHLph7MbBDK4he10TWhophJFDO_TuNiAI7P2ojVFMC_RUU27_JIp1wzV80htzu6S9CXar9SisuzM1MTWd59nuJV6NqQkjfxWmpgt1xZSDZ2q6YJxKeWHhEU_-heQ18fWV64aZeywVHAX6i_wZkoPAawaP_E3AM3peEJiaIPP7XYnfj_izydYfJ4VAxfRMi-cOFP6_WL-169uqfwEAAP__RRSOzw) across the Persian Gulf, the Sea of Oman, and the Red Sea, a move that could compound one of the worst oil market disruptions in history. The U.S. military announced its naval blockade of Iranian ports has been fully implemented, completely [halting Iran's seaborne trade](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykUL2SmCAYfBrscAA50IIijd2lTel8yqd-CYIDnI55-ox5hSu22dnZv1-f0ydQoLj9hANdXdMU8S4Ba8U8UYZY94xQy445nZniQicEmJRQhgvNpZk8UHgm3Xi3IirsGnTSWtN13WD7Znf9rKUValnAvJCzXH1vZwHzKvygh4bc6ya0NFIII_u2t_NHjyDQ-kEbo5gW6Kmm3P5OFOuOa3jShbld0tEEt9d6Ftb9YGpkarzvu41wQajJw_NKmBrfAKZGoZka5QdT47uMIPI1wLah5xeWgoHXTFh4TRwv8Mi_Co9wPXwOafnzEhR5qRmo8rTyPeXj6y9TY5OdP28KgYqxTIvtAAr_y9VvPXo59S8AAP__sgGLcQ). At least nine vessels have now been turned around, with none breaking through. President Trump said Wednesday that the war is ["very close to over,"](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGOrCAQRb9GdxhEBVyweBt3_bazNNVQtkwjEMA2PV8_YZL5gtlVTlUq99yP23oD66x__IcDVdnC6vHKDkvBtNoEvuwJoeQdU4jJem0jOFgZZZzQkfR8NWDdex1bozZEhkOLqheCD8MwC9nuivaaa8FAGypmo7mctMR52vi0jYwBba2q3-jY855S3stOivskESgKM4-cs2akaGwJqfsM1pcdN_cOL0ydDkfr1F5KzM3wr2FLw5brujp_19Wi7isJyZmGLdWmYYuzLyR3Fx6_8xkNFMzkzBXrJxgk9ZbsIR3nFynpPCKJCBpJAffMJGkPw9DLmbZJmXhZ52zmohnp4wDrfnKVP5X5Uuw7AAD__4Lwin4) with in-person U.S.-Iran peace talks potentially resuming this week. Vice President Vance expressed optimism after leading the highest-level U.S.-Iran negotiations in nearly 50 years. Uranium enrichment remains a key sticking point, with the U.S. seeking a 20-year suspension and Iran offering five years.
## New Video Shows Principal Tackling Armed Gunman
A high school principal in Oklahoma is shown on newly released security footage tackling an armed gunman inside the Pauls Valley High School lobby last week, preventing what police say could have been a mass shooting at the school. [You can see the video here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpCAURp9GOwwgg_4FxTZ2s-2W5gpXuTsIBhjNvP3GzWZf4O9OcpOb75xfz_kJFChuP2FHU9c0R7xKwFoxz5QhVp8RavGY05EpWjogwCy51IwrJvTsgMJnVq0zK6LEvkUjhkH3ff81jK03owLl0CkBegV4oHWWLxr4sKDQ6rG0ZO5vXAktONdi7MZheYwIHAf3pbSWjeLoqKbc_U4Uq8c1fNKJubNpb4PxtR6l6X80cmrkdF1XFxd7W9z3Rk43NnJ6F_aP0iuATzswT5tnxfqUAvsvxwqc6NiLXGGBTiysgn3didj2jjtEVnyqLNsIfS9Grdts3HFRCFT00Ci-7UDh77b6raCnkX8CAAD__xBHjWc). The principal, Kirk Moore, was shot in the leg during the confrontation but survived. The video captures Moore charging the suspect from behind and pinning him down on a bench. Another school employee then helped disarm the man. Victor Hawkins, 20, a former student, has been charged with shooting with intent to kill and other felonies. Investigators say he told them he wanted to [carry out an attack](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunTAQRL8GOpBtjDGFizR0N21KtBcv1xstGNkOiL-PeMX7gdeNNNKMzvnzml9ATPvnN2zoyhrnHa_MWAqmmRLsJSSEkgOmeCTaFzqAYVZCmUboRprZA_E969q7FVFhV6OTw2C6rhsHWwcn_duLdVXa6g5X4a0BHOS4iFECLAJqcs-a0NJIIYy0rR3evUUQOPhRG6MqLdBTian9G2kvAVe-44mpXeJWswulHLnqflVqqtR0XVd7Q4jxaSs1PTiVmiAVWhifeJLH2OQQr9wc8I9zcwIz3s03X6NkZ3uh-74NZeM6OX9cxEzZDJUWnw2Iv87Lj4ydTv0PAAD__7M6gMs) modeled on the 1999 Columbine massacre.
## Ranking: Where Young Adults Still Live at Home
A new ranking of which states have the [most young adults still living with their parents](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGupCAUQL9GOwwCAq-g2MbubbuluaPX4W5QCNzRzN9vZn_h9SfnJOfP9_INlOh8_oYDA-95OfFuCZmxLlTh5FgRuEWsuVQ6VyqQYFFSWSGNGO2yAaX3Yvot7IgKdY9hdM5qrb-c72NA4633q1y1H6fJaK_BrXLaEXaFTj96Ch-bNKMdpbSjH7x7TB5Botu-jLWqMxI34lyHv5lOjrind76wDms--hQic2md_tWpuVPzfd_DRe0FaYVCDIkaf8BOzQeUgpu4I1YU7_w6nwK2V-ImEl0ojtxY3MRRcESqokDFk1un5r6GrdyUEjXrOiOfB1D6X-cfLbuC-hcAAP__m-qCwA) shows that New Jersey tops the nation, with 44.1% of adults ages 18-34 still living at home, the highest rate in the country by a wide margin. High-cost Northeastern and coastal states consistently dominate the top of the rankings, while more affordable states like North Dakota, at just 12.3%, fall to the bottom. Nationally, about one in three young adults now live with their parents, a figure that remains well above historical norms, despite easing slightly from the 2020 pandemic peak. Rising housing costs continue to delay independence for many young Americans, and experts say this trend now appears structural rather than temporary. [See the full ranking map here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGupCAUQL9GOwwCAq-g2MbubbuluaPX4W5QCNzRzN9vZn_h9SfnJOfP9_INlOh8_oYDA-95OfFuCZmxLlTh5FgRuEWsuVQ6VyqQYFFSWSGNGO2yAaX3Yvot7IgKdY9hdM5qrb-c72NA4633q1y1H6fJaK_BrXLaEXaFTj96Ch-bNKMdpbSjH7x7TB5Botu-jLWqMxI34lyHv5lOjrind76wDms--hQic2md_tWpuVPzfd_DRe0FaYVCDIkaf8BOzQeUgpu4I1YU7_w6nwK2V-ImEl0ojtxY3MRRcESqokDFk1un5r6GrdyUEjXrOiOfB1D6X-cfLbuC-hcAAP__m-qCwA).

Right now, MAGA holds a crushing 9-0 stranglehold on the court. Flip these two seats and that becomes 7-2 and suddenly a path opens up to reclaim the court entirely.
3 more seats are up for grabs in May 2028. Win these two seats next month, and Democrats could flip this critical swing state court to a 5-4 majority in '28 -- just months before the presidential election.

If you care about preserving the NH Advantage — no income tax, lower burdens on families and small businesses — please listen now and share with friends in your town while the conversation is still fresh. I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places.

That's how countries are lost.

Slowly. Then all at once.

But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope...

There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged.

_And it shouldn 't even exist. _

**Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.**
That alone felt like a miracle.

Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have.

Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down.

And yet...

_They stepped up anyway. _

About that time, Charlie called me.

He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent.

"Andrew, we've got to move faster."

I told him we were. He stopped me.

"No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I actually laughed.

"Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said. "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000."

I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools.

We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet.

But Charlie wasn't fazed.

_" We'll figure it out." _

That was him.

He didn't wait for perfect conditions.

Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... _we lose everything. _

And now?

Less than a year later...

**We 're in 3,300 schools. **

**Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. **

**Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. **

_That shouldn 't be possible. _

Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day.

And yet... it's still happening.

_But Peter, here 's the part you need to understand: _

This is not a victory. It's a foothold.

_Because in the other 87% of schools? _

There is no resistance. None.

Just one-sided propaganda from the Left.

One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them.

That's the reality.

The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are.

The question is whether it's enough.

Because right now, the students stepping up through Club America...

They're not the majority. _They 're the exception. _

They're the ones willing to take the heat.

The ones willing to stand alone.

The ones willing to risk being targeted just to say: _" I love this country." _

And every time one of those students raises their hand...

We have a choice.

Back them. _Or leave them on their own. _

**Because when a student starts a chapter, we send them an activism kit -- with American flags. Pocket Constitutions. Leadership tools. **

Everything they need to actually stand their ground.

Not symbolically. For real.

They've already made the decision to lead.

All they're waiting on... is you and me.

**Each activism kit costs $25. That 's it. **

$25 to make sure one student doesn't have to stand alone against the Left in a hostile school.

$25 to put real tools in their hands.

$25 to push back -- even if it's one campus at a time.

Club America isn't slowing down. It's accelerating.

Because every day, more students are stepping forward.

Not because it's easy or popular...

_But because they know what 's at stake. _

They're starting chapters in schools where they were told not to.

They're speaking truth in classrooms where the Left once went unchallenged.

They're choosing courage in places designed to make them conform.

And they're not alone.

They're finding each other. They're bringing more students with them every day.

They're building something real -- rooted in faith and freedom, grounded in truth, and unafraid to say that America is worth defending.

Not from the top down... _But from the ground up. _

One student. One school. One chapter at a time.

And Peter -- that's exactly how we take this country back.

But only if we move fast enough.

Because the Left isn't slowing down. They're not taking a break.

They're not afraid to push their anti-American ideas in every classroom they're in.

And if we don't match that urgency... if we don't meet that moment with equal conviction...

Then the generational window Charlie Kirk opened to save our country closes.

And once it closes... It closes for good.

That's what's at stake.

Let's not waste this moment. Let's back our brave students -- _while it still matters. _

**P.S.** I need you to hear this clearly...

Charlie Kirk wasn't just dreaming big when he called me last year about Club America's progress.

He was warning us:

"The enemy is moving younger. They're coming after students earlier. **_We don 't have time to wait._" **

And he was right. Look around.

Club America may be in 13% of high schools...

_But in the other 87%? _

There is no pushback against the Left.

No one telling those kids the truth.

Just a Leftist pipeline -- from classroom... to belief... to voting booth.

And once that pipeline is complete... _It 's over. _

**Peter, this is one of the last places a patriot like you can stop it before it 's too late to save our country. **

Not "if things keep going this way." Right now. And the scariest part? It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms. High schools. Colleges. Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped. If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: " What happened to this country?" You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly. Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything... The other side is doing something far more dangerous. They're raising the next generation. Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places. That's how countries are lost. Slowly. Then all at once. But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope... There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged. And it shouldn 't even exist. Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools. That alone felt like a miracle. Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have. Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down. And yet... They stepped up anyway. About that time, Charlie called me. He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent. "Andrew, we've got to move faster." I told him we were. He stopped me. "No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools." I actually laughed. "Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America." "Okay," he said. "How many are there?" "About 27,000." And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000." I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet. But Charlie wasn't fazed. " We'll figure it out." That was him. He didn't wait for perfect conditions. Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... we lose everything. And now? Less than a year later... We 're in 3,300 schools. Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. That shouldn 't be possible. Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day. And yet... it's still happening. But Peter, here 's the part you need to understand: This is not a victory. It's a foothold. Because in the other 87% of schools? There is no resistance. None. Just one-sided propaganda from the Left. One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them. That's the reality. The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are. The question is whether it's enough. Because right now, the students stepping up through Club America... They're not the majority. They 're the exception. They're the ones willing to take the heat. The ones willing to stand alone. The ones willing to risk being targeted just to say: " I love this country." And every time one of those students raises their hand... We have a choice. Back them. Or leave them on their own. Because when a student starts a chapter, we send them an activism kit -- with American flags. Pocket Constitutions. Leadership tools. Everything they need to actually stand their ground. Not symbolically. For real. They've already made the decision to lead. All they're waiting on... is you and me. Each activism kit costs $25. That 's it. $25 to make sure one student doesn't have to stand alone against the Left in a hostile school. $25 to put real tools in their hands. $25 to push back -- even if it's one campus at a time. But here's what gives me hope, Peter... Club America isn't slowing down. It's accelerating. Because every day, more students are stepping forward. Not because it's easy or popular... But because they know what 's at stake. They're starting chapters in schools where they were told not to. They're speaking truth in classrooms where the Left once went unchallenged. They're choosing courage in places designed to make them conform. And they're not alone. They're finding each other. They're bringing more students with them every day. They're building something real -- rooted in faith and freedom, grounded in truth, and unafraid to say that America is worth defending. That's how movements are built. Not from the top down... But from the ground up. One student. One school. One chapter at a time. And Peter -- that's exactly how we take this country back. But only if we move fast enough. Because the Left isn't slowing down. They're not taking a break. They're not afraid to push their anti-American ideas in every classroom they're in. And if we don't match that urgency... if we don't meet that moment with equal conviction... Then the generational window Charlie Kirk opened to save our country closes. And once it closes... No one telling those kids the truth. Just a Leftist pipeline -- from classroom... to belief... to voting booth. And once that pipeline is complete... It 's over. Peter, this is one of the last places a patriot like you can stop it before it 's too late to save our country. Patriot,

I recently came across a striking statistic.

**72% of J6 defendants were military veterans or first responders.**

_Is this how our criminal justice system thanks them for their service?_

I’ve always honored those who serve. We are living the American dream _because_ of them. The way these patriots were treated is a grave injustice.

And while President Trump has pardoned almost all of the J6 defendants, they still haven’t received justice.

The lives and reputations of these patriots remain shattered from the lost years to the consistent government and mainstream media smear campaign they endured.

That’s why I’m proud to support Stand in the Gap.

* Harassment on social media and in their personal lives
* Strained family relationships due to lost time in prison
* And even homelessness.

**Stand in the Gap is committed to being a comprehensive support system for J6 defendants and their families by providing essential resources to help these American patriots heal physically, mentally, emotionally, and spiritually.**

Stand in the Gap believes in second chances, providing support to individuals transitioning back into society after incarceration, and working towards a more forward-thinking and restorative prison system that sends non-violent offenders into the world better off than they were when they went in.

Through their programs, partnerships, and advocacy efforts, they are making a lasting impact on the lives of those in need.

**There are nearly 1,600 Americans who are looking for a second chance.**

Let’s show these patriots they’re not forgotten.

# Armstrong For Congress - April Campaign Updates

Hey Peter, I wanted to take a minute to bring you up to speed on where things stand and what the next stretch of this campaign will look like.
Over the past couple of months, most of our focus has been on getting the foundation in place so this campaign can actually hold up under pressure.
That means building the right team and making sure we are not just showing up, but doing this in a way that can compete across the whole district.
Now you’re going to start seeing a lot more of us out in the open.
**WHERE I’LL BE:**
We’ve got a full calendar coming together, and I hope you can make it out to something nearby in the upcoming weeks:
**Thu April 16 – Ladysmith and Rice Lake** Will be joining Rusk County @ 6pm and Barron County Dems @ 7:30pm at their respective offices.
**Fri April 17 – Wabeno** I’ll be joining a Tribal Nations conversation at Potawatomi Casino alongside Francesca Hong, Ginger Murray, Yee Leng Xiong, and others.
**Sat April 18 – Medford** Plan to stop by the Pro-Democracy Rally on the way back from Wabeno on Saturday morning – 9:00 am-12:00pm at the corner of Hwy 13 and Hwy 64.
**Sun April 19 – St. Croix Falls** Polk and Burnett County Dueholm Event at Chateau St. Croix Winery, a great chance to connect with folks from across western Wisconsin.
**Sun April 25 – Marathon County** WI 7th District Convention, with more details coming soon.
We’ll keep adding more events as we go, so if you want to stay up to date, check the events page on the website.
**THE KICKOFF:**
---
|
---
| |
Last month’s kickoff said a lot about what we’re building.
We filled the room, and nobody treated it like a drop-in.
People hung around, pulled up chairs, got into real conversations about what’s going on in their lives and what they want to see change.
Nashville recording artist Trey Taylor played a great set, and the whole night just flowed.
It felt like people showed up for each other as much as they showed up for the campaign.
That’s the kind of foundation that actually holds when things get tough.
That’s what we’re building toward.
**WHAT WE NEED RIGHT NOW:**
We’re getting ready to start ballot signature collection, and this is one of those moments that quietly decides whether a campaign moves forward or stalls out.
If we don’t collect the signatures, none of the rest of this matters. It is as simple as that.
So we’re asking people to step in and help carry that work.
If you’re willing to be part of it, send a note to hello@armstrongforcongress.com, and we’ll get you set up with training and everything you need to get started.
For those anxious to get started today, please visit the website and click the “[Nomination Form](https://armstrongforwisconsin.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=cf02e39423b56c583c783bf1a&id=e806040ed3&e=0c0d11993f)” button at the top of the home page to download the form.
**WHAT WE ARE SEEING ON THE GROUND:**
I feel good about where this is headed because you can already see the shift happening in our communities.
In our recent elections, Chris Taylor’s race saw about a twenty-point swing toward progressives.
In St. Croix County, candidates like Danielle McIntosh and Jared Bell got across the line.
New Richmond voters decided to stick with science and keep fluoridation in place.And even in races that were closer, we held onto strong voices like Marilyn Duerst and Neal Melby.
Getting on the ballot is the first step. From there, it becomes about building something strong enough to flip this seat in a year where the maps are changing, and the opportunity is right in front of us.
I appreciate you being part of this.
Thanks, Chris ~:|

body:
Virginia Tests the Limits of Mid-Decade Redistricting - By Justin Riemer, President, USGI, and Marshal Trigg, Junior Counsel, USGI

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/grantdemocracy/grant-report-february-5-12772509?e=c16f400a56)
---
[|
---](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=d3db04aa06&e=c16f400a56)
| | **Virginia Tests the Limits of Mid-Decade Redistricting**
**By Justin Riemer, President, USGI, and Marshal Trigg, Junior Counsel, USGI** On Tuesday, Virginia voters will answer a [seemingly innocuous question](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=f0379ce468&e=c16f400a56) that carries enormous consequences for the balance of power in Congress: Should the General Assembly be allowed to temporarily redraw the state’s congressional districts to “restore fairness in upcoming elections”? In 2020, Virginia voters overwhelmingly [approved](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=cd9a15b137&e=c16f400a56) a state constitutional amendment creating a bipartisan redistricting commission, thus explicitly taking mapmaking out of the legislature’s hands. To undo that arrangement, even temporarily, Democrats needed to amend the constitution again and do so in time for this year’s midterms. Virginia’s amendment process requires passage of the amendment in two consecutive legislative sessions with a general election in between, followed by a public referendum. Virginia threaded that needle at breakneck speed, passing the amendment in October 2025 and again in January 2026, then scheduling the April 21 special election. Newly-sworn in Governor Spanberger signed the [proposed map](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=d08adae782&e=c16f400a56)—which will likely move the state from a 6-to-5 to 10-to-1 Democratic configuration—into law on February 20, contingent on voter approval.What followed was a legal ping-pong match without recent precedent in Virginia: [multiple lawsuits](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=4502ff0af1&e=c16f400a56), a [lower court blocking](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=dbcd5698c2&e=c16f400a56) the referendum [twice](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=4acdc27af8&e=c16f400a56) and on different grounds, the [state Supreme Court staying](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=9b0ada8957&e=c16f400a56) those rulings [twice](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=d2e82748cf&e=c16f400a56), and contradictory orders that left local officials confused enough that [Lynchburg had to sue for clarification](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=0494c48a90&e=c16f400a56).In short, Republicans argue principally that Democrats had improperly shoehorned the amendment into a special session originally convened to address the state budget and failed to pass the amendment “before” the intervening general election as required since over a million Virginians had already cast early ballots by the time of the first legislative vote. Indeed, the principle behind the intervening-election requirement is that voters should be able to weigh the candidate’s vote on an amendment when deciding whether to vote for that candidate. Republican challengers have additionally argued that the ballot language about “restoring fairness” is misleading, or that the amendment could never properly be enacted at all, given state constitutional constraints on mid-decade districting and compactness requirements. Defendants counter that courts lack the power to enforce internal legislative procedure, that the intervening-election requirement refers to Election Day itself, and dismisses the ballot language issue as mere “disagreements over wording.” Here’s where it stands today. The vote is well-underway (early voting began March 6 and runs through April 18, with Election Day on April 21), but the Supreme Court of Virginia has not ruled on whether the amendment is valid. A Richmond circuit court will hear arguments on a Republican challenge on April 20, the day before the election. Meanwhile, final briefs in the main case before the Supreme Court are due April 23, two days _after_ the election. Obviously a “no” vote will put the matter to rest and likely moot the litigations. And if the courts ultimately invalidate the amendment, a “yes” vote becomes a nullity. If neither occurs, then the new map takes effect for November, potentially flipping four congressional seats.Despite a barrage of litigation, thus far, courts have not intervened to stop states’ mid-decade redistricting, although pending challenges remain in Missouri, and will undoubtedly be brought in Florida assuming it enacts new lines. If voters vote “yes” on April 21, it’s entirely conceivable that the Supreme Court of Virginia’s decision could determine which party will control the House of Representatives after November’s election.
---
| | | | |
---
| | **Alabama** Governor Ivey signed the [Alabama Post-Election Audit Act](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=9d2da6b4b8&e=c16f400a56) __ into law. This law will require every county to conduct a [post-election audit](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=52271e39eb&e=c16f400a56) in one countywide and one statewide race in one precinct after every general election. **Arizona** The state is [implementing a new ID verification process](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=2a23654c8c&e=c16f400a56) for voters who are returning mail-in ballots in person. Rather than relying solely on signature verification, voters may present identification to confirm their identity at drop-off. The change is intended to streamline ballot processing and reduce delays in post-election counting.[An audit of the 2024 presidential election in Arizona](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=c95510738b&e=c16f400a56) identified 28 ballots as potentially unlawful. In 25 of those, individuals voted in Arizona and then cast a second ballot in another state for the same election. One ballot was attributed to a deceased individual.**Colorado** The State Court of Appeals [vacated the nine-year sentence of former elections clerk](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=95f9f9b9a7&e=c16f400a56) Tina Peters after it determined that the sentence was wrongly based on Peters’ exercise of her First Amendment right to speech. Peters was convicted of four felony and three misdemeanor crimes after she brought an unauthorized individual into a secure area to examine the voting equipment. She will be resentenced by a district court judge. **Georgia** Georgia election boards are facing uncertainty as [a state law banning the use of QR codes](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=a97ec9075f&e=c16f400a56) on ballots approaches its July deadline, with officials across all 159 counties awaiting guidance on how to comply.**Mississippi** Governor Reeves signed the SHIELD Act into law. This law will [require county registrars to check an applicant’s information through the federal government’s SAVE](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=62e1d55bef&e=c16f400a56) program unless it is available through the state driver’s license identification system. This law is slated to take effect on July 1. **Nebraska** Governor Pillen has [signed](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=2c4e32b231&e=c16f400a56) a bill that would ban foreign funding of ballot issue campaigns in the state.**Nevada** The Washoe County Registrar [released results](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=83d1a7b64b&e=c16f400a56) from its last 16 months of voter list maintenance, reporting over 75,000 confirmation notices sent and over 55,000 voters moved to inactive status. **New Hampshire** Governor Ayotte signed a [bill](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=04f45c9195&e=c16f400a56) eliminating the use of high school and college IDs for voting. Under the new law, voters must present a qualifying form of ID, such as a driver’s license from any state, a non-driver ID, a U.S. military ID, or a U.S. passport, to verify their identity.**New Jersey** A state court [invalidated a ballot cast by a voter who had moved to Chicago](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=af3a8266a9&e=c16f400a56) but continued voting in a local New Jersey election, ultimately affecting the outcome of a closely contested municipal race. Although such violations are typically referred to law enforcement and election officials, the court declined to do so here.Governor Sherrill [signed a new bill into law](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=56f83e4e51&e=c16f400a56) that will allow early voting in May municipal non-partisan elections. A state court [dismissed long-running voter fraud charges](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=818e02a3b4&e=c16f400a56) against Paterson Councilman Alex Mendez, ending a six-year prosecution stemming from alleged mail-in ballot fraud in the 2020 municipal election. The Attorney General’s Office stated it disagrees with the decision and is evaluating options. **New York** Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections (RITE) and Rep. Claudia Tenney [have requested comprehensive records and data](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=bf49308f88&e=c16f400a56) from the New York State Board of Elections (NYSBOE) in order to identify shortcomings in the state’s voter registration system. This [recent letter](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=3aecd29c5f&e=c16f400a56) comes after the NYSBOE failed to respond to RITE’s [November 2025 letter](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=bab7711ab6&e=c16f400a56) identifying violations of the Help America Vote Act (HAVA). RITE and Rep. Tenney say they are prepared to enforce compliance in federal court if NYSBOE does not respond by the May 7 deadline for production.**Texas** At least three counties [received administrative subpoenas](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=75eb29c0b8&e=c16f400a56) from the U.S. Department of Homeland Security for the voter files seeking detailed voter records for specific individuals. The subpoenas follow Texas’s earlier decision to provide voter roll information to the U.S. Department of Justice.**Utah** Ballotpedia [published a post-session roundup](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=04b626d69a&e=c16f400a56) of Utah’s 2026 legislative activity, highlighting the enactment of 14 election-related bills signed into law before the legislature adjourned in March. The summary spotlights HB 209, which requires documentary proof of citizenship for voter registration in state and local elections while permitting federal-only voting for applicants who do not provide such documentation. It also notes a mandated review of existing voter rolls using state and federal data to identify potential noncitizens.Lt. Governor Henderson [notified more than 300,000 Utah voters](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=344a3ee8a9&e=c16f400a56) that their voter registration records will soon become public. The notices follow enactment of Senate Bill 153, which revises the privacy classification of voter registration records. Beginning May 25, these records—including names, addresses, party affiliation, and precinct information—will be available upon request, while personal identifying information will remain protected.**Virginia** Governor Spanberger signed a bill [adding the state to the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=8bf4524c09&e=c16f400a56), a multistate agreement to award presidential electors to the winner of the national popular vote rather than the Electoral College outcome. With Virginia’s addition, the compact now includes states representing 222 electoral votes, still short of the 270 needed for it to take effect.**West Virginia** Governor Morrisey [signed a bill tightening voter residency requirements](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=13b9058172&e=c16f400a56), requiring individuals registering to vote to demonstrate that they intend to remain in the state “indefinitely.”**Wisconsin** Governor Evers [signed a bill](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=13c7752b34&e=c16f400a56) aligning its presidential election certification timeline with federal deadlines. The change brings state law into conformity with the Electoral Count Reform Act, adopted after the 2020 election to reduce opportunities for post-election disruption. At the same time, Governor Evers vetoed a separate Republican-backed bill that would have required the state elections commission to adjudicate complaints against itself under the Help America Vote Act, and mandated audits aimed at identifying potential noncitizen voters.Wausau’s mayor [will not face criminal charges](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=c10cd35d79&e=c16f400a56) for removing an absentee ballot drop box from outside city hall in September 2024, a special prosecutor announced last week. The Milwaukee Election Commission [reported that 269 absentee ballots were delivered the morning after the April 7 election](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=45ce695f98&e=c16f400a56), rendering them ineligible to be counted under Wisconsin law, which requires ballots to be received by Election Day.Election officials in Madison and Dane Counties [counted 23 late-arriving ballots](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=7c537e4af9&e=c16f400a56) in the recent Wisconsin Supreme Court race, despite objections from Republican officials who argued the ballots should be rejected under state law. The ballots were received after polls closed at 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.**Wyoming** Weston County Clerk Becky Hadlock was [arrested after a special prosecutor filed two additional felony charges](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=ab62a4db99&e=c16f400a56) related to her conduct surrounding the 2024 General Election. The charges include one count of violating the election code as an official and one count of falsifying election documents, each punishable by up to five years in prison. These new charges represent a third legal case against Hadlock, who already faced a misdemeanor charge for defying a legislative subpoena and a separate proceeding seeking her removal from office for misconduct and malfeasance.

In 2020, Virginia voters overwhelmingly a state constitutional amendment creating a bipartisan redistricting commission, thus explicitly taking mapmaking out of the legislature’s hands. To undo that arrangement, even temporarily, Democrats needed to amend the constitution again and do so in time for this year’s midterms. Virginia’s amendment process requires passage of the amendment in two consecutive legislative sessions with a general election in between, followed by a public referendum. Virginia threaded that needle at breakneck speed, passing the amendment in October 2025 and again in January 2026, then scheduling the April 21 special election. Newly-sworn in Governor Spanberger signed the —which will likely move the state from a 6-to-5 to 10-to-1 Democratic configuration—into law on February 20, contingent on voter approval.What followed was a legal ping-pong match without recent precedent in Virginia: , a the referendum and on different grounds, the those rulings , and contradictory orders that left local officials confused enough that short, Republicans argue principally that Democrats had improperly shoehorned the amendment into a special session originally convened to address the state budget and failed to pass the amendment “before” the intervening general election as required since over a million Virginians had already cast early ballots by the time of the first legislative vote. Indeed, the principle behind the intervening-election requirement is that voters should be able to weigh the candidate’s vote on an amendment when deciding whether to vote for that candidate. Republican challengers have additionally argued that the ballot language about “restoring fairness” is misleading, or that the amendment could never properly be enacted at all, given state constitutional constraints on mid-decade districting and compactness requirements. Defendants counter that courts lack the power to enforce internal legislative procedure, that the intervening-election requirement refers to Election Day itself, and dismisses the ballot language issue as mere “disagreements over wording.” Here’s where it stands today. The vote is well-underway (early voting began March 6 and runs through April 18, with Election Day on April 21), but the Supreme Court of Virginia has not ruled on whether the amendment is valid. A Richmond circuit court will hear arguments on a Republican challenge on April 20, the day before the election. Meanwhile, final briefs in the main case before the Supreme Court are due April 23, two days after the election. Obviously a “no” vote will put the matter to rest and likely moot the litigations. And if the courts ultimately invalidate the amendment, a “yes” vote becomes a nullity. If neither occurs, then the new map takes effect for November, potentially flipping four congressional seats.Despite a barrage of litigation, thus far, courts have not intervened to stop states’ mid-decade redistricting, although pending challenges remain in Missouri, and will undoubtedly be brought in Florida assuming it enacts new lines. Friend,
Recently a new wave of attacks has come my way. While they don't surprise me, they do disappoint.
Not because they sting. But because every dollar spent tearing me down is a dollar not spent talking about _you_. Your family, your gas prices, your border, your future.
There's plenty I could say about my opponents. But like I told them straight to their face in our debate several weeks ago: **my focus isn't on them. It never has been. It's on YOU.**
**That's not a campaign line. It's who I am.**
As a Christ-follower, a husband, and a father, I've built my life and my service on **integrity, humility, and conviction** , the same values American families build their lives on every single day.
_Those aren't words I dust off at election time. _They're what has guided every decision I've made as Attorney General, and they're what will guide me in Washington when the fights get hard and the pressure to compromise comes from every direction.
**I've never wavered in fighting for America's values. Not when it was easy, not when it was costly, and I won't start wavering now just because the attacks are getting personal.**
**Here's what I know:** _the people running these attacks are afraid._ They're afraid of a senator who answers to Americans; not to lobbyists, not to party leaders, not to the loudest voices on cable news.
**May 19 is around the corner. By then, I fully intend to earn your vote, win in November, and get to Washington to fulfill every promise I've made to you.**
**But I need your help getting there.** This is a grassroots campaign going up against big money and bigger lies. Your support, whatever you can give, is what keeps us in the fight.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. subject: Following up from yesterday…
body:
---
Hi Derek, I know I reached out last night, but I wanted to follow up with you: We came up six percent short of our $250,000 mid-month goal. After I reached out, this team got us three percent closer to our goal, and I'm grateful. But we need to close that gap today, before midnight. So I hope you’ll give me a chance to explain why goals like these matter, especially right now. This is a longer message, but it is important and, in a minute, I’m going to [**personally ask for your support.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-april-2026?amount=7&refcode=em_20260416_6737_fr&refcode2=6737_22930333_pRt6NB&akid=6737%2E22930333%2EpRt6NB) **[CHIP IN](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-april-2026?amount=7refcode=em_20260416_6737_fr&refcode2=6737_22930333_pRt6NB&akid=6737%2E22930333%2EpRt6NB)** November’s midterm elections are right around the corner, and we know that to win anywhere, we have to organize everywhere. That’s exactly what we’re doing. This year, we launched our new When We Count program, which is already working to register more than 250,000 new Democratic voters in battleground states. Democrats have won or overperformed in **_264 out of 295**_ key elections since Trump took office. These victories were only possible because we made historic investments in organizing, registering new Democratic voters, and our state party infrastructure. Grassroots supporters like you made those investments happen. And Derek, along with all the other work that we’re leading ahead of November, the DNC is also holding Trump accountable in the courts. We filed a new lawsuit to stop Trump from illegally restricting vote-by-mail and our legal team is using every tool at their disposal to defend Americans’ voting rights. As you can imagine, all of this work takes a massive amount of resources. This team has always stepped up when we’ve asked for your help, and I’m asking for your support one more time to keep funding our work. [**That’s why, if this work inspires you too, I hope you’ll consider pitching in $7 to the DNC today. subject: NEXT WEEK: Lunch & Learn: Faith, Ethics, and AI. Join Us on Capitol Hill, April 22
body:
Faith leaders and AI policy converge on Capitol Hill. Join us April 22 at the Dirksen Senate Building.

| [ ](https://ar.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=08a015b56b&e=a07d75591f)
---
| April 22, 2026 * 12:00 PM ET * Dirksen Senate Building, Room G50 | [Register Now](https://ar.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=dfde72373f&e=a07d75591f)
---|---
As artificial intelligence rapidly reshapes our world, it raises urgent questions not only about technology, but about humanity -- our values, responsibilities, and purpose.

**Join us on Wednesday, April 22 at 12pm** for lunch and hear from a diverse group of faith leaders exploring how spiritual and moral frameworks can help guide the development and use of AI.
| [Save Your Spot](https://ar.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=24c0a289b4&e=a07d75591f)
---
|
---
What We'll Explore | -> How do faith traditions approach the ethical questions raised by AI?
---
-> What does human dignity mean in an age of intelligent machines?

That program is already firing on all cylinders. But there's a problem: They're facing a critical funding gap.
If that gap isn't closed immediately, the program could start stalling--or worse--breakdown altogether at the exact moment it needs to be strongest.
That's why they reached out to us. And it's why we're coming to you, Peter.
We've proven what works. We've proven we can win. Now we need to step in and make sure Georgia doesn't slip away. Because here's the reality:
Democrats are on a hot streak and we need fuel to keep the fire burning.
Georgia's judicial elections are nonpartisan and held during primaries. That means many Democratic voters won't know which candidates to support, unless we tell them.

body:
#

Friends —
This afternoon, the 2026 NRA convention kicks off just a few hours’ drive from Uvalde, Texas.
Daniel Defense — the manufacturer of the assault weapon found in Robb Elementary School — is an exhibitor and giving “MAJOR discounts” to NRA members.
Special guests in years past have included Donald Trump, Senator Ted Cruz, and Governor Greg Abbott.
And if history is any guide, NRA CEO Doug Hamlin and others will peddle the fiction that the only way to stop gun violence in America is by selling more guns.
This is what we’re up against — a gun lobby and the politicians they pay are so committed to the profits of gun manufacturers that the impact on our communities is simply the cost of doing business.
And it’s clear that even in the wake of some of the deadliest mass shootings ever, they will keep pushing to sell more guns and block calls for action.
It’s despicable. But we have the tools to fight back.
When we started this work 13 years ago, most politicians — even Democrats — were afraid to take on the NRA. But slowly, surely, we have been making it clear that standing up to the NRA and the gun lobby is the path to victory.
**So please. As the NRA begins its convention, help us fight back. Especially today:**

clean_body: | | | | | | Friends- We are so excited that these affordability bills have been signed into law in Virginia. Though many bills are still going through the legislative process, we are one step closer to a Virginia you can afford. Affordable Healthcare: == (Helmer): Site neutral payments for health insurance companies == (Sullivan): Directs SCC to apply to the federal government for extension of reinsurance waiver, and remove 20% premium reduction cap == (Callsen) & == (Rouse): Requires a PBM to use the pass-through pricing model and prohibits PBM from deriving income outside of management fee; requires regular SCC reports Consumer Protection: == (Pekarsky) & == (Reaser): Click to Cancel A Virginia You Can Afford: == (Lucas) & == (Ward): Raises Minimum Wage == (McClure) & == (Carroll Foy): Raises Farmworker Minimum Wage == (Pope Adams) & == (McPike): Directs Department of Taxation to create free tax filing program == (Torian) & == (McPike): Expands eligibility for RetirePath == (Martinez): Prohibits use of credit cards as payment for sports betting Affordable Housing: == (Shin): Restricts partnership, corporation, or trust from buying single family home == (Cohen): ADUs Statewide (mandatory) == (Sewell): Requires localities with 20,000+ people to allow one and two-family dwellings and townhouses by right == (Simonds): Allows locality to authorize a zoning administrator to use administrative process to approve rezoning for affordable housing Affordable Childcare: == (Locke) & == (Sewell): Dedicated Child Care Funding Formula == (McClure) & == (Aird): Creates employee childcare assistance pilot program Affordable Energy: == (Bagby) & == (Sullivan): Increases energy battery storage targets for utilities == (Carroll Foy) & == (Sewell): Provides that localities may require solar be built on canopies over parking lots == (VanValkenburg) & == (Callsen): Increases RPS requirements for Dominion to deploy rooftop/behind the meter solar or wind; expands PPA access; encourages solar development on previously developed sites == (Deeds) & == (Shin): Requires the SCC to establish by regulation a cost-sharing mechanism for the recovery of fuel costs, including the costs of purchased power == (Shin): States it will be the policy of the Commonwealth that no investor-owned utility shall engage in practices that distort wholesale energy markets (uneconomic dispatch) Make sure to keep an eye on your inbox and follow us on social media for more legislative updates! | == == == | We are so grateful for your continued support in the fight for an affordable Virginia.
